headline: No shared execution or data channels are exposed; pairwise risks are effectively blocked, with only compliance uncertainty from undocumented residency/retention policies.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent exposes a shared communication channel, filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout bridge. Agent A cannot read/write files or use MCP; agent B likewise cannot read/write files or use MCP. With no ingestion path, prompt injection between them is provably blocked from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP server, this verdict no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared workspaces.
Disable any future clipboard bridge between them.
Avoid routing one agent's raw text into the other's prompt.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show no filesystem read/write, no network egress, no clipboard, and no declared data classes touched. There is no documented path for sensitive data to flow from one agent to the other or out to a third party, so leakage is not plausible from the profiles provided.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem access or network egress, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF sensitive data classes are added to either profile, this verdict no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep both agents offline.
Do not mount shared sensitive workspaces.
Do not assign secrets or regulated data to either agent.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before enabling any data-bearing integration.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles show no overlapping write capabilities: both agents have write_filesystem=false, modify_git_state=false, and no subprocess or shell execution. Without shared mutable resources or write authority, capability conflict is not a plausible pathway.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory or git repository, conflict risk must be reassessed.
IF an orchestrator later provides shared locking-free mutable state, this verdict no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Do not grant overlapping OAuth scopes or database writes.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: No evidence shows either agent consuming the other's outputs as authoritative, and neither profile exposes action-taking authority such as shell, browser, or API calls. With no downstream actuation path, cascading error from one agent into the other is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF B begins to treat A's text as authoritative input, this verdict changes.
IF either agent is later given action-taking tools, cascading-error risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Do not auto-forward outputs from A into B.
Keep both agents advisory-only.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for any future handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: Compliance risk is limited to documentation gaps: both agents are open-source, docs-only, and no residency, retention, or regulated data handling is specified. Because no sensitive data class is declared, there is no concrete breach pathway; however, the absence of policy detail means a small compliance gap remains if regulated data is later introduced.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or other regulated data is assigned to either agent, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF retention or residency policies are later documented as conflicting, severity increases.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data to either agent.
Document retention and residency policies before deployment.
Confirm vendor/legal terms for any future data flow.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
